name: Hollins Bottom Autumn Season
summary: Six weeks living and working lightly on a hill farm turned land project, with forty or so others. Talking is most of the point. No fee.
description:
Hollins Bottom is a hundred and ten acres of rough grazing and planted woodland that has been run as a land project since 2009. Every autumn we take in around forty people for six weeks, from the last week of September to early November.

The days have a fixed shape and the shape is gentle. Breakfast at eight. Two hours of light work in the morning: sorting apples, mending fence, planting whips, cooking. Lunch is long. The afternoons are for walking, reading, or sleeping. At five there is a circle in the big barn, thirty or forty of us, and that is where the season actually happens. People talk about what they are carrying and other people listen. It goes on as long as it needs to. Supper follows.

Nobody teaches anything. Two of us who have lived here a long time hold the circle and are around during the day if someone wants a conversation. That is the extent of it.

You do not need to have done anything like this before. Most people have not. You need to be willing to talk in a room of forty people and to be quiet while others do, and to get up at a reasonable hour.

The work is light and the walking is optional. This is not a place to come to be pushed.
practical: Six weeks, late September to early November. No fee; the project runs on donations and most people give something at the end. Shared rooms in the farmhouse and two bunkhouses, forty beds. All meals, mostly from the land. Bring waterproofs, boots, and warm layers; it is cold by October. Trains to Skipton, then we collect on the Saturday. No mobile signal in the valley; there is wifi in the barn.
